title: Properties
intro: Pick a property, read and fill in its profile, add a property (and the checks that stop a duplicate), import its rent roll, rename it, and archive or delete it.

topics.title: Specific Property
topics.intro: One property at a time: its loans, its NOI, its profile, its rent roll and its documents.

steps.title: The property list
steps.text: Click Specific Property at the top of Home, then pick a property in the list. Next to a name the list says “senior + mezz” (two loans), “in a pooled loan” or “no loan yet”.

marks.label: Whole Portfolio
marks.text: Back to the overview of the whole book.

marks.label: Specific Property
marks.text: This view.

marks.label: Select a property
marks.text: Click it and pick a property; its page opens below.

marks.label: Add Loan
marks.text: A new loan on this property (see “A loan’s page”).

marks.label: Add Property
marks.text: A new property, by its name (topic “Add a property”).

marks.label: Edit
marks.text: Opens this property’s profile (topic “The profile”).

marks.label: Remove
marks.text: Archives this property and all its loans — it asks first. Un-archive it from Home’s Archived strip.

marks.label: Refi Calculator
marks.text: The refinance for this property.

marks.label: The property’s page
marks.text: Starts here, under the bar (next step).

marks.label: Portfolio tab
marks.text: This tab. Tools open in tabs next to it, from the “+”.
Opens Underwriting, the Calendar or Data Health in a new tab.

marks.label: Data
marks.text: Back up, restore, and Excel export / import (see the Home chapter).

marks.label: Fetch live rate
marks.text: Gets today’s index values.

marks.label: Settings
marks.text: See the Settings chapter.

marks.label: Properties
marks.text: How many properties are in the book (archived ones don’t count).

steps.title: A property’s page
steps.text: A property with a loan opens on this page. From the top: the loan’s tiles and rate notice, the NOI box, the profile, the rent roll and the documents. Further down: the Loan Record and the schedule (chapter “A loan’s page”).

marks.label: Tiles
marks.text: The loan’s main figures.

marks.label: Rate notice
marks.text: How a floating or hybrid rate is set this month.

marks.label: NOI box
marks.text: The property’s NOI, DSCR, debt yield and LTV, and where the NOI came from.

marks.label: Property profile
marks.text: Click to open it: the property’s facts (topic “The profile”).

marks.label: Build operating model
marks.text: Opens the property in Underwriting.

marks.label: Rent roll summary
marks.text: Units, occupancy and rents from its rent roll (topic “Rent roll”).

marks.label: Import rent roll
marks.text: Brings in its rent roll (topic “Rent roll”).

marks.label: Documents
marks.text: The property’s saved files (see the Documents chapter).

marks.label: What you are adding
marks.text: The kind of file — or let the app detect it.

marks.label: Add files
marks.text: Saves files to the property’s folder.

topics.title: Add a property
topics.intro: Add Property needs only a name — its loans, T12 and documents come later. Before it makes one, it checks you don’t have it already.

steps.title: The Add Property window
steps.text: Click Add Property, type the name and click Create.

marks.label: Property name
marks.text: The property’s name — enough to start.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Closes it; nothing is made.

marks.label: Create
marks.text: Checks the name, then adds the property.

steps.title: No name
steps.text: Create with no name and it asks for one.

marks.label: Enter a property name
marks.text: Type a name, then Create.

steps.title: Created
steps.text: A made-up “Birch Commons (example)”. It joins the list at once, marked “no loan yet”, and gets its own folder for its files. (A name you already have is refused with a short message.)

marks.label: In the list
marks.text: Birch Commons (example) · no loan yet. Its page opens below (topic “A property with no loan”).

marks.label: Add Loan
marks.text: Its first loan.

marks.label: Add Property
marks.text: Another property.

marks.label: Edit (greyed)
marks.text: Edit, Remove and Refi Calculator are for a property with a loan. This page has its own Archive.

marks.label: Remove (greyed)
marks.text: See Archive on the page instead.

marks.label: Refi Calculator (greyed)
marks.text: No loan to refinance yet.

steps.title: A similar name
steps.text: A name that looks like one you have (here “Birch Commons”) asks first: open the one you have, or make the new one anyway.

marks.label: Looks like
marks.text: The property (or properties) it looks like.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Nothing is made.

marks.label: Create anyway
marks.text: It is a different property: make it.

marks.label: Open it
marks.text: It is the same property: open the one you have.

steps.title: An archived name
steps.text: A name you archived before (here the made-up “Old Mill (example)”) asks: bring the old one back with its data, or start fresh — which deletes the archived one’s data for good (it asks again).

marks.label: Already exists
marks.text: And when it was archived.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Nothing changes.

marks.label: Start fresh
marks.text: Deletes the archived property’s data and makes a new, empty one.

marks.label: Restore it
marks.text: Un-archives the old one, with all its data.

steps.title: A loan’s name
steps.text: A name that is one of your loans, or an address (here the sample “Avalon WP (Mezz)”), is not a new property: it offers to add a loan to that property instead.

marks.label: Whose it is
marks.text: Which property the name belongs to.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Nothing is made.

marks.label: Add a loan to it
marks.text: Opens a new loan form on that property.

topics.title: A property with no loan
topics.intro: A new property, or one whose loans were all removed, has its own page: never blank.

steps.title: The page
steps.text: Its name with “No loan yet”, its NOI box, its profile, its rent roll and its documents. Removed or paid-off loans, if any, are listed here with Restore. (The profile opens by itself on this page; here it is closed to show the whole page.)

marks.label: No loan yet
marks.text: The property has no active loan.

marks.label: + Add the first loan
marks.text: Opens a loan form with this property filled in.

marks.label: Archive
marks.text: Takes it out of Home and the totals (topic “Archive and delete”).

marks.label: NOI box
marks.text: Its NOI and value (next step).

marks.label: Profile
marks.text: Its facts — click to open or close (topic “The profile”).

marks.label: Rent roll summary
marks.text: Topic “Rent roll”.

marks.label: Import rent roll
marks.text: Brings in its rent roll.

marks.label: Documents
marks.text: Its saved files (see the Documents chapter).

marks.label: What you are adding
marks.text: The kind of file — or let the app detect it.

marks.label: Add files
marks.text: Saves files to its folder.

steps.title: Its NOI box
steps.text: With no loan there is no DSCR, debt yield or LTV — the box says so. It shows the NOI and the value at a cap rate (the last loan’s, or the default).

marks.label: Property NOI
marks.text: Its yearly NOI, once there is one.

marks.label: Value
marks.text: NOI ÷ cap rate.

marks.label: Cap rate
marks.text: The last loan’s cap rate, or the default.

marks.label: Debt
marks.text: None — no loan.

marks.label: Open in Underwriting
marks.text: Opens this property in Underwriting, to upload its T12.

marks.label: Where the NOI comes from
marks.text: Here: no NOI yet — upload its T12 or type one in its profile.

steps.title: + Add the first loan
steps.text: Opens the Add Loan form with the property’s name filled in. Fill in the loan and save; the page becomes its loan page. Cancel comes back here.

marks.label: Add Loan
marks.text: The loan form — every field is explained in “A loan’s page” › Add a loan.

marks.label: Property Name
marks.text: Already this property.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Back to the property’s page.

marks.label: Save Loan
marks.text: Saves the loan on this property.

marks.label: Loan Terms
marks.text: The terms from the loan papers.

marks.label: Escrows & Reserves
marks.text: Monthly escrows.

marks.label: Additional Fees
marks.text: Monthly fees.

steps.title: Open in Underwriting
steps.text: Opens Underwriting in a tab of its own, with this property chosen — upload its T12 there (see the Underwriting chapter).

marks.label: Property
marks.text: Already this property.

marks.label: The T12 box
marks.text: Drop its T12 here, or click “choose a file”.

marks.label: Units
marks.text: Its units (filled from the rent roll once there is one).

marks.label: Gross potential rent
marks.text: A whole year’s rent at market.

marks.label: Average rent
marks.text: Or the average monthly rent; the app works out the year.

topics.title: The profile
topics.intro: The property’s facts that don’t change often. Each field saves as soon as you leave it.

steps.title: Every field
steps.text: Edit (in the bar at the top) opens the profile; on the page you can also click its title. Shown here on a sample property. A faded value is read from the loan until you type your own.

marks.label: Property profile
marks.text: Click to open or close it. Next to it: what is still missing, or “Profile complete”.

marks.label: Property name
marks.text: Changing it renames the property everywhere (topic “Rename”).

marks.label: history
marks.text: This field’s changes (old → new, who, when).

marks.label: Address / market
marks.text: Changes the address on all its loans.

marks.label: Residential units
marks.text: Whole number.

marks.label: Commercial units
marks.text: Shops or restaurants: in the NOI, not in per-unit figures.

marks.label: Rentable sq ft
marks.text: Whole number.

marks.label: Year built
marks.text: 1800 to this year.

marks.label: Acquisition date
marks.text: When it was bought.

marks.label: Manager
marks.text: Living, or the third-party manager.

marks.label: Data source
marks.text: Living Yardi, Third-party or Manual.

marks.label: Yardi property code
marks.text: Its code in Yardi.

marks.label: NOI override
marks.text: Typed by you only. Replaces the T12’s NOI everywhere. Clear it to go back.

marks.label: Notes
marks.text: Anything else.

steps.title: Fill it in
steps.text: Type into a field and leave it (Tab or click away): it is saved, with who and when under it. Units, sq ft and year built are checked first — a wrong number is not saved. With the name, units, acquisition date and manager set, the profile is complete.

marks.label: Profile complete
marks.text: Every needed fact is in.

marks.label: Address / market
marks.text: Typed: a made-up address.

marks.label: Residential units
marks.text: Typed: 12.

marks.label: Last changed
marks.text: Who changed it, and when.

marks.label: history (1)
marks.text: Its changes so far (last step of this topic).

marks.label: Year built
marks.text: Typed: 1988. A year before 1800 or after this year is refused.

marks.label: Acquisition date
marks.text: Picked from the calendar.

marks.label: Manager
marks.text: Typed: Living.

marks.label: Data source
marks.text: Picked: Manual.

marks.label: NOI (annual, entered)
marks.text: Only for a property with no loan: an NOI to use until it has a T12 (next step).

marks.label: NOI override
marks.text: Replaces any other NOI (step after next).

steps.title: An entered NOI
steps.text: With no T12 yet, type the NOI here. The NOI box uses it at once and says so. Once a T12 is uploaded, the T12’s NOI is used instead.

marks.label: Property NOI
marks.text: The NOI just typed.

marks.label: Value
marks.text: That NOI ÷ the cap rate.

marks.label: Cap rate
marks.text: The default cap rate (no loan has given one).

marks.label: Debt
marks.text: None.

marks.label: Open in Underwriting
marks.text: Upload its T12 there.

marks.label: Your entered NOI
marks.text: Says the NOI is the one typed in the profile — no T12 yet.

steps.title: The NOI override
steps.text: An override is typed by you only and wins over everything — the T12, the entered NOI. DSCR, debt yield, Home and the refinance all use it. Clear the field to go back.

marks.label: Property NOI
marks.text: Now the override.

marks.label: Value
marks.text: Worked out again from the override.

marks.label: Cap rate
marks.text: Unchanged.

marks.label: Debt
marks.text: None.

marks.label: Open in Underwriting
marks.text: Upload its T12 there.

marks.label: Your NOI override
marks.text: Says the override is in use.

steps.title: History on a field
steps.text: A field with changes on record has “history (N)” next to its name. Click it: every change, old → new, who, when and where from. Here Residential units was changed from 12 to 14.

marks.label: Which field
marks.text: The field and the property.

marks.label: When
marks.text: When it changed.

marks.label: Old → new
marks.text: What it was and what it became.

marks.label: Who
marks.text: Who changed it.

marks.label: Where from
marks.text: Typed, a rent roll, the assistant, a loan agreement…

marks.label: Close
marks.text: Closes the window.

topics.title: Rent roll
topics.intro: Import the property’s rent roll (a Yardi export, Excel or CSV) to see its units, occupancy and rents. Shown with a made-up 12-unit rent roll.

steps.title: No rent roll yet
steps.text: The Rent roll summary is on every property’s page. Click Import rent roll and pick the file in the window that opens.

marks.label: Rent roll summary
marks.text: Empty until a rent roll is imported.

marks.label: Import rent roll
marks.text: Opens your computer’s file window: pick the rent roll.

steps.title: Which part is whose
steps.text: The app reads the file and lists its parts (a file can hold several properties). Opened from a property, its part is set to that property. Check it, then click Import.

marks.label: The file
marks.text: Its name and how many parts it has.

marks.label: What the app found
marks.text: Which part is set to which property.
Closes it; nothing is saved.

marks.label: Use this part
marks.text: Ticked: this part is imported.

marks.label: Which property
marks.text: The property this part belongs to — or “Add as a new property”.

marks.label: + another property
marks.text: The same part for one more property.

marks.label: Note
marks.text: Nothing is saved until you click Import.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Closes it; nothing is saved.

marks.label: Import
marks.text: Saves the file to the property’s folder and reads its summary.

steps.title: The summary
steps.text: The summary: units, occupied, vacant, the average market and in-place rents, and the square feet. Update brings in a newer rent roll. Underwriting fills its units and rent from it.

marks.label: From
marks.text: The file it came from.

marks.label: Update
marks.text: Replace it with a newer rent roll.

marks.label: Units
marks.text: Residential units in the rent roll.

marks.label: Occupied
marks.text: Units with a resident.

marks.label: Vacant
marks.text: Empty units.

marks.label: Avg market
marks.text: Average market rent a month.

marks.label: Avg in-place
marks.text: Average rent actually charged a month.

marks.label: Sq ft
marks.text: Total square feet of the units.

topics.title: Rename a property
topics.intro: Change the name in its profile. One name, everywhere.

steps.title: Type the new name
steps.text: Open the profile, type the new name in Property name and leave the field (Tab or click away). On a property with loans the name changes on every loan (a mezz keeps “(Mezz)”), and its files and chats move with it. If the new name already has files of its own, it asks first: put them together, or don’t rename.

marks.label: Property name
marks.text: The new name, saved.

marks.label: history (2)
marks.text: The old name and the new one.

marks.label: Address / market
marks.text: Changing it changes the address on all its loans.

steps.title: Everywhere
steps.text: The page, the property list and Home all use the new name at once.

marks.label: The new name
marks.text: On its page — and in the property list.

marks.label: + Add the first loan
marks.text: A loan on the renamed property.

marks.label: Archive
marks.text: Next topic.

topics.title: Archive and delete
topics.intro: Archive takes a property out of Home, the totals and the assistant, and keeps everything. Delete permanently removes it for good — only an archived property can be deleted.

steps.title: Archive
steps.text: On a property with no loan, click Archive on its page. (A property with loans: Remove in the bar at the top archives it with its loans.) It asks first.

marks.label: What happens
marks.text: It leaves Home, the totals and the assistant.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Keeps it.

marks.label: Archive
marks.text: Archives it.

steps.title: An archived property
steps.text: Its page says “archived”. Un-archive brings it back as it was. Delete permanently removes it for good.

marks.label: archived
marks.text: Out of Home, the totals and the assistant.

marks.label: Un-archive
marks.text: Back in Home and the totals, with all its data.

marks.label: Delete permanently
marks.text: Removes it for good (it asks first).

steps.title: Un-archive
steps.text: Click Un-archive: it is back, with its profile, rent roll and files.

marks.label: Back
marks.text: No longer archived.

marks.label: Archive
marks.text: Archive it again (needed before it can be deleted).

steps.title: Delete permanently
steps.text: Archive it again, then click Delete permanently. The window lists exactly what goes — its loans, T12, documents, chats, profile and figures. The automatic backups keep a copy.

marks.label: What goes
marks.text: Everything about the property, listed.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Keeps it (archived).

marks.label: Delete permanently
marks.text: Deletes it for good and goes back to Home.

steps.title: Home’s Archived strip
steps.text: Every archived property is listed near the bottom of Home (here the made-up “Old Mill (example)”). Click its name to un-archive it, or the bin to delete it for good.

marks.label: Un-archive
marks.text: Click the name: it is back in Home and the totals.

marks.label: Delete permanently
marks.text: Removes it and its files for good (it asks first).
